# The appointments Andvari made — and who is keeping them

One myth is a story. A cycle of myths is a specification. Read Andvari's cycle in order and the industries fall out of it one by one.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Andvari
- **Pantheon:** Norse
- **Domain of influence:** Dwarf, Guardian of Gold
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Home & Lifestyle · Commerce & Governance · Energy & Natural World
- **Strongest seat:** Gems, Jewelry & Luxury Materials
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 31 of 542

## The Cycle, Read Forward

### Gems, Jewelry & Luxury Materials — through *The Otter's Ransom*

Óðinn, Loki, and Hœnir were traveling when they came to a waterfall, and there they saw an otter eating a salmon on the bank, its eyes shut.  Loki killed it with a stone and boasted of a double catch — otter and fish at one cast.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *Andvaranaut — the cursed ring whose hoard dooms every owner.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

### Legal, Justice & Compliance — through *The Net of Rán*

Völsunga saga gives the fullest account of the catching.  Loki went to Rán, the sea-queen who drowns sailors, and borrowed her net, then came to the waterfall called Andvarafors.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The curse that follows the ring — ownership without justice, paid for in lives.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. The trade thinks it is optimizing a process. It is re-enacting a charter.

### Mining & Natural Resources — through *The Curse on the Ring*

Stripped of everything, Andvari did the only thing left to a dwarf with nothing: he spoke.  Reginsmál's prose preserves the curse as the tradition's own words: the gold that Gustr had owned — Gustr, 'Gust', the other name the prose gives the dwarf — would be the death of two brothers, and would bring strife to eight of the kin-line — eight ættlingar — and no man would ever have joy of his wealth.

The atlas states the seat in one line: *The gold of Andvarafors, hoarded in the waterfall and sunk at last in the Rhine.* The story above is the long version of the same sentence. That is the cycle working: story becomes duty, duty becomes trade.

## The Theme That Runs the Cycle

Andvari's dossier is a single episode and its long echo: one afternoon's extortion at a waterfall, and a curse that runs through the rest of the Völsung cycle like poison through water. Reginsmál's prose, Snorri's Skáldskaparmál, and Völsunga saga all tell the catching; everything after — Fáfnir's dragon, Sigurðr's sword, the gold sunk in the Rhine — is the curse working itself out.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

The atlas is not a horoscope. Seats are earned from the sources — argued, weighted, published — and every one of them can be challenged at the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). A match that cannot survive an argument does not survive review. That is the whole trick: the patterns are claims, and claims can be tested.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in gems, jewelry & luxury materials, legal, justice & compliance, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/andvari/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
